# ecoSynthesis

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of `ecoSynthesis` is to assist users in the synthesis of 
cross-referencing information between two classification systems.
The examples in this package focus on ecosystem classifications, and
specifically on cross-referencing from local classifications to
a global standard classification, but functions are designed to work
with any pair of classification systems.

The process of cross-reference implies a source classification and 
a target classification, where the target classification might have
a broader scope than the source. Elements in the source classification 
can be interpreted as directly related to one or more elements in the 
target classification. This relationship can be quantified as membership
values, where the source element has memberships between 0 and 100% to each
element of the target classification. 

![Diagram](man/figures/diagram-concept-match.png)

The membership table (long format) looks like this (assuming all other 
possible pairs have 0% membership).

 Source Classification | Target Classification | Membership
|---|---|---|
| Concept A | Concept Z | 100% |
| Concept B | Concept W | 60% |
| Concept B | Concept Z | 40% |


## Installation

You can install the development version of ecoSynthesis from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Ecosystem-Indicators-Workflows/ecoSynthesis")
```

## Example

This is a basic example which shows you how to solve a common problem:

```{r example}
library(ecoSynthesis)

input_table <- data.frame(
    local_name = c("Semi-deciduous Forest","Deciduous Forest","Wet Montane Forest","Dry Montane Forest"),
    efg1 = c("T1.1", "T1.2", "T1.1", "T1.2"),
    memb1 = c(80,80,70,50),
    efg2 = c("T1.2", "T1.1", "T1.3", "T1.3"),
    memb2 = c(20,20,30,50)
)

membership_table(
    input_table, 
    "local_name",
    c("efg1","efg2"),
    c("memb1","memb2"),
    target="T1.3")
```

This package implements recommended methods from:

> IUCN (2025). Standards, methods and guidelines for cross-referencing ecosystem classifications and maps to the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology. Version 1.0. Keith, D. A., Dayaram, A., Driver, A., Ferrer-Paris, J. R., Francis, R., Hay, S., Murray, N. J., Nicholson, E., Santos, J., Skowno, A. L. & Tozer, M. G. (Eds.). Gland, Switzerland: IUCN. ISBN: 978-2-8317-2348-8. DOI:10.2305/CPPC6126.

This package in in the very early stages of development.
